bull.b: The sharp FY2026 revenue and earnings rebound demonstrates substantial operating leverage and stronger market demand. If elevated profitability persists, SanDisk should have greater capacity to fund technology, capacity expansion and shareholder returns through the next several quarters.

Multi-year NBMs create unusually strong forward demand visibility and deepen strategic relationships with major Datacenter and Edge customers. Their duration and contractual structure can reduce dependence on spot NAND sales and support more predictable revenue over the next two to six months.

Free cash flow converting nearly one-for-one from net income indicates that the current earnings rebound is producing substantial liquidity rather than only accounting profit. That cash strengthens financial flexibility for investment, debt management and capital returns during market fluctuations.

bear.b: The recent turnaround follows several years of losses and negative free cash flow, showing that SanDisk's earnings power remains highly sensitive to NAND pricing, demand and industry conditions. This history makes current margins and cash generation less certain to sustain across a full cycle.

Weak consumer revenue remains a fundamental headwind for the branded and device-oriented portions of the business, even though full-year consumer revenue increased. A recovery is not expected until 2027, leaving near-term mix and demand exposed to prolonged PC and smartphone adjustment.

Moving toward large, multi-year NBM contracts improves visibility but concentrates revenue and execution exposure among fewer customers. Changes in the priorities, purchasing plans or financial condition of a major partner could therefore have an outsized effect on SanDisk's results.
